subject: maths
title: Days, Weeks, Months and Time
seo_title: Year 1 Time Worksheets: Days of the Week, Months, Seasons and O’clock (Free, Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the duration and sequence of events using years, months, weeks, days and hours
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on time, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M1M03): morning, afternoon and night, days of the week, yesterday and tomorrow, months and Australian seasons, which takes longer, and o’clock and half past. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Yesterday is before today. Tomorrow is after today.
key_sub: 7 days in a week, 12 months in a year. In Australia, summer is December to February and winter is June to August. Long hand on the 12: o’clock. Long hand on the 6: half past.
body_html:
Morning, afternoon and night

Every day goes in the same order: morning, afternoon, night. We eat breakfast in the morning. School finishes in the afternoon. We sleep at night.

Use first, next, then and last to tell things in order. Before means earlier. After means later.

Example 1

Leo has a bath. Then he reads a story. What does he do first?

“Then” tells us the story comes later. The bath comes first.

Answer: has a bath

Days of the week

There are 7 days in a week. Monday to Friday are school days. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

WordMeans
yesterdaythe day before today
todaythis day
tomorrowthe day after today
Example 2

Today is Sunday. What day is tomorrow?

Tomorrow is the day after today. After Sunday a new week starts.

Answer: Monday

Months and seasons in Australia

There are 12 months in a year, from January to December. There are 4 seasons. Each season has 3 months.

SeasonMonths in Australia
summerDecember, January, February
autumnMarch, April, May
winterJune, July, August
springSeptember, October, November

Christmas is in summer in Australia. In England and the USA it is winter at Christmas, because their seasons are the other way round.

Which takes longer?

A minute is short. An hour is 60 minutes. A day is 24 hours. A week is 7 days. A month is about 4 weeks. A year is 12 months.

Example 3

Mia stays for 2 days. Kai stays for 1 week. Who stays longer?

1 week is 7 days. 7 days is more than 2 days.

Answer: Kai

O’clock and half past

On an analog clock, the short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Long hand on the 12: it is o’clock. Long hand on the 6: it is half past.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying July is summer and Christmas is in winterIn Australia, summer is December to February. July is winter
Mixing up yesterday and tomorrowYesterday is before today. Tomorrow is after today
Thinking 2 days is longer than 1 week because 2 is biggerLook at the word too. 1 week is 7 days
Reading half past 3 as half past 4Use the number the short hand has gone past: half past 3
Mixing up the two handsShort hand = hour. Long hand on the 12 = o’clock, on the 6 = half past

faq.q: What time and calendar skills does Year 1 learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 1 students describe the duration and order of events using years, months, weeks, days and hours (AC9M1M03). They use words like morning, yesterday and tomorrow, name the days and months, and read o’clock and half past times.

faq.q: What are the seasons in Australia?
faq.a: Summer is December, January and February. Autumn is March to May, winter is June to August and spring is September to November.

faq.q: Why is Christmas in summer in Australia?
faq.a: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere, so its seasons are the opposite of England and the USA. December is the start of summer here.

faq.q: How can I help my Year 1 child learn the days of the week and months?
faq.a: Say them in order each day and talk about yesterday, today and tomorrow, like “Today is Monday, so tomorrow is Tuesday.” Mark birthdays, school holidays and sport days on a family calendar.

sets.title: Morning, afternoon and night: the order of events

items.q: The sun comes up. When is it?
items.e: The sun comes up at the start of the day. That is the morning.

items.q: The moon and stars are out. When is it?
items.e: We see the moon and stars when it is dark. That is night.

items.q: Noah eats breakfast. When is it?
items.e: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. We eat it in the morning.

items.q: Ruby goes to sleep in bed. When is it?
items.e: We sleep when it is dark, at night.

items.q: School finishes. It is home time. When is it?
items.e: School finishes after lunch. That is in the afternoon.

items.q: We eat lunch at school. What comes after lunch?
items.e: Lunch is in the middle of the day. After lunch comes the afternoon.

items.q: William brushes his teeth just before bed. When is it?
items.e: Bedtime is at the end of the day. So it is at night.

items.q: Which part of the day is missing?
items.e: The day goes morning, afternoon, then night.

items.q: Which part of the day is missing?
items.e: The day starts with the morning. Then comes the afternoon, then night.

items.q: What happens first?
items.e: Follow the arrows from the left. The first card is wake up.

items.q: What happens last?
items.e: Follow the arrows to the end. The last card is catch the bus. (Get up is first, not last.)

items.q: What happens just after “water it”?
items.e: Find “water it”. Follow the arrow to the next card: it grows. (Plant a seed comes before.)

items.q: What happens just before “it washes away”?
items.e: Find “it washes away”. Look at the card just before it: a wave comes.

items.q: What goes in the card with the ?
items.e: It is after a bath and before sleep, so it is at night: read a story. Waking up, breakfast and school are in the morning.

items.q: What goes in the card with the ?
items.e: At school, recess comes first. Then lunch. Then it is home time.

items.q: Cooper eats dinner. After dinner, he has a bath. What does he do first?
items.e: “After dinner, he has a bath” means dinner comes first. So he eats dinner first.

items.q: You put on your socks ____ your shoes.
items.e: Socks go on first. Then shoes go on top. So socks go on before your shoes.

items.q: You dry your hands ____ you wash them.
items.e: First you wash your hands. Then you dry them. So you dry them after you wash them.

items.q: Put the pictures in order for one day. Start with the morning.
items.e: B is the morning (the sun comes up). C is the afternoon (the sun is high). A is night (the moon). The order is B, C, A.

items.q: Charlotte wakes up. Then she goes to school. Then she goes to bed. What does she do in the middle?
items.e: First she wakes up. In the middle she goes to school. Last, she goes to bed.

sets.title: Days of the week: yesterday, today and tomorrow

items.q: How many days are in a week?
items.e: Count the days: Monday to Sunday. There are 7 days in a week. (5 is only the school days.)

items.q: Which day is missing?
items.e: Tuesday comes before the gap and Thursday comes after it. The missing day is Wednesday.

items.q: Which day is missing?
items.e: Friday comes before the gap and Sunday comes after it. The missing day is Saturday.

items.q: Which day comes just after Monday?
items.e: Say the days in order: Monday, Tuesday. Tuesday comes just after Monday. (Sunday comes before.)

items.q: Which day comes just before Friday?
items.e: Say the days in order: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. (Saturday comes after Friday.)

items.q: Which day comes just after Sunday?
items.e: Sunday is the last day of the week. Then a new week starts with Monday.

items.q: Which two days are the weekend?
items.e: Most children go to school Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

items.q: On which days do most children go to school?
items.e: School days are Monday to Friday. That is 5 days. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

items.q: Today is Tuesday. Wednesday is …
items.e: Wednesday comes just after today. The day after today is tomorrow.

items.q: Today is Tuesday. Monday was …
items.e: Monday comes just before today. The day before today is yesterday.

items.q: Today is Thursday. What day will it be tomorrow?
items.e: Tomorrow is the day after today. The day after Thursday is Friday. (Wednesday was yesterday.)

items.q: Today is Monday. What day was it yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before today. The day before Monday is Sunday. (Tuesday is tomorrow.)

items.q: Today is Saturday. What day will it be tomorrow?
items.e: Tomorrow is the day after today. The day after Saturday is Sunday. (Friday was yesterday.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day was it yesterday?
items.e: Yesterday is the day before today. The day before Wednesday is Tuesday. (Thursday is tomorrow.)

items.q: Yesterday was Friday. What day is it today?
items.e: Today is the day after yesterday. The day after Friday is Saturday. (Thursday is the day before Friday, not after.)

items.q: Tomorrow will be Monday. What day is it today?
items.e: Today is the day before tomorrow. The day before Monday is Sunday. (Tuesday is after Monday.)

items.q: Today is Wednesday. What day is the day after tomorrow?
items.e: Tomorrow is Thursday. The day after that is Friday.

items.q: Today is Friday. Isla’s footy game is on Sunday. How many sleeps until the game?
items.e: Sleep 1: Friday night, then it is Saturday. Sleep 2: Saturday night, then it is Sunday. That is 2 sleeps.

items.q: Today is Monday. Library day is Thursday. How many days away is it?
items.e: Count on from Monday: Tuesday (1), Wednesday (2), Thursday (3). Library day is 3 days away. (Do not count Monday itself.)

items.q: How many school days are in a week?
items.e: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That is 5 school days. (7 is every day of the week.)

items.q: How many months are in a year?
items.e: Count them: January to December. There are 12 months. (7 is days in a week. 4 is seasons.)

items.q: Which is the first month of the year?
items.e: The year starts with January. December is the last month.

items.q: Which month is missing?
items.e: April comes before the gap and June comes after it. The missing month is May.

items.q: Which month is missing?
items.e: September comes before the gap and November comes after it. The missing month is October.

items.q: Which month comes just after March?
items.e: Say the months in order: February, March, April, May.

items.q: Which month comes just before June?
items.e: Say the months in order: April, May, June, July.

items.q: Which month comes just after December?
items.e: December is the last month. Then a new year starts with January.

items.q: How many seasons are in a year?
items.e: Summer, autumn, winter and spring: 4 seasons. (12 is the number of months.)

items.q: Which season is missing?
items.e: In Australia the seasons go summer, autumn, winter, spring. June, July and August are winter.

items.q: In Australia, which season has the hottest days?
items.e: Summer is the hottest season. In Australia it is December, January and February.

items.q: In Australia, which season is January?
items.e: In Australia, summer is December, January and February. So January is summer. (January is winter in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

items.q: In Australia, which season is July?
items.e: In Australia, winter is June, July and August. So July is winter. (July is summer in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

items.q: Christmas Day is in December. In Australia, which season is it?
items.e: In Australia, summer is December, January and February. So December is summer. (December is winter in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

items.q: Lots of flowers open in September. In Australia, which season is it?
items.e: In Australia, spring is September, October and November. So September is spring. (September is autumn in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

items.q: Which months are autumn in Australia?
items.e: In Australia, autumn is March, April and May. (September, October and November is autumn in the north of the world, not here.)

items.q: Which months are winter in Australia?
items.e: In Australia, winter is June, July and August. (December, January and February is winter in the north of the world. Here it is summer.)

items.q: Which season comes just after winter?
items.e: Summer, autumn, winter, spring. Spring comes after winter. (Autumn comes before winter.)

items.q: Which season comes just after summer?
items.e: Summer, autumn, winter, spring. Autumn comes after summer. (Spring comes before summer.)

items.q: Jack’s birthday is in July. In Australia, which season is it?
items.e: In Australia, winter is June, July and August. So July is winter. (July is summer in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

items.q: School starts again in February after the long holidays. In Australia, which season is February?
items.e: In Australia, summer is December, January and February. So February is summer. (February is winter in countries in the north of the world, like England, not in Australia.)

sets.title: Which takes longer? Minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: In 1 minute the long hand moves 1 small step. In 1 hour it goes all the way round. So 1 hour is longer than 1 minute.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: 1 week is 7 days. So 1 week is longer than 1 day.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: 1 month is about 4 weeks. So 1 month is longer than 1 week.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: 1 year is 12 months. So 1 year is longer than 1 month.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: A week is 7 days. A month is about 4 weeks. A year is 12 months. So 1 day is the shortest.

items.q: Which order goes from shortest to longest?
items.e: A minute is very short. An hour is longer. A day has 24 hours. So: minute, hour, day.

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: Breakfast takes a few minutes. A night’s sleep takes many hours. So a night’s sleep takes longer.

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: Brushing teeth takes about 2 minutes. A school day takes about 6 hours. So a school day takes longer.

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: Recess is a short break, about 20 to 30 minutes. A whole school day is about 6 hours. So a school day takes longer.

items.q: Which takes longer?
items.e: A weekend is 2 days. Summer holidays are about 6 weeks. So summer holidays take longer.

items.q: About how long does it take to wash your hands?
items.e: Wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry. It is quick: about 1 minute.

items.q: About how long should you brush your teeth?
items.e: Dentists say to brush for about 2 minutes. 2 hours would be far too long.

items.q: About how long is a school day?
items.e: School starts in the morning and ends in the afternoon. That is about 6 hours.

items.q: About how long are the summer holidays in Australia?
items.e: The summer holidays go from December to the end of January. That is about 6 weeks.

items.q: A sunflower seed grows into a big flower. About how long does it take?
items.e: Plants grow slowly. A sunflower takes about 3 months to grow tall and flower.

items.q: Which takes the longest?
items.e: A school week has 5 school days. A school year has many weeks. So a school year is the longest.

items.q: Chloe sleeps for 10 hours. Grace sleeps for 9 hours. Who sleeps longer?
items.e: Both are in hours. 10 is more than 9. So Chloe sleeps longer.

items.q: A cricket match lasts 3 hours. A netball game lasts 1 hour. Which is longer?
items.e: Both are in hours. 3 hours is more than 1 hour. So the cricket match is longer.

items.q: Ethan reads for 1 hour. Ava reads for 20 minutes. Who reads longer?
items.e: Look at the words, not only the numbers. 1 hour is 60 minutes. 60 minutes is more than 20 minutes. So Ethan reads longer. (20 is bigger than 1, but minutes are short.)

items.q: Oliver stays at the beach for 2 days. Aarav stays for 1 week. Who stays longer?
items.e: 1 week is 7 days. 7 days is more than 2 days. So Aarav stays longer. (2 is bigger than 1, but a week is longer than a day.)

sets.title: O’clock and half past in your day

items.e: The long hand is on the 6, so it is half past. The short hand has gone past the 6. It is half past 6, not half past 7.
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 7. It is 7 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 9. It is 9 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 11. It is 11 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand is on the 6, so it is half past. The short hand has gone past the 12. It is half past 12, not half past 1.
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 3. It is 3 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand is on the 6, so it is half past. The short hand has gone past the 4. It is half past 4, not half past 5.
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 6. It is 6 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand is on the 6, so it is half past. The short hand has gone past the 7. It is half past 7, not half past 8.
The long hand is on the 12, so it is o’clock. The short hand points to the 10. It is 10 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
Clock C has the long hand on the 6 and the short hand just past the 8. It shows half past 8. Clock D has the hands swapped. Clock A shows half past 9.
Clock A has the long hand on the 12 and the short hand on the 2. It shows 2 o’clock. Clock B has the hands swapped.
Clock D has the long hand on the 6 and the short hand just past the 11. It shows half past 11. Clock C has the hands swapped. Clock A shows half past 12.
In 1 hour the short hand moves on to the next number. 3 o’clock → 4 o’clock. (2 o’clock was 1 hour ago.)
In half an hour the long hand goes from the 12 down to the 6. 9 o’clock → half past 9. (10 o’clock is 1 hour later.)
In half an hour the long hand goes from the 6 up to the 12. A new hour starts: 5 o’clock. (Half past 5 is 1 hour later.)
Half past 10 comes before 11 o’clock. So Noah is early.
9 o’clock comes after half past 8. The bus has gone. So Ruby is late.
Count the hours: 2 o’clock to 3 o’clock is 1, 3 o’clock to 4 o’clock is 2. It is 2 hours. (4 is the end time, not how long.)
The long hand goes from the 12 to the 6. That is half of the way round: half an hour.
